articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran Designation Update
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a new designation update related to Iran on November 9, 2026.

Further details regarding the specific entities or individuals targeted by this designation were not immediately available, but such actions typically aim to counter Iran's destabilizing activities, including its nuclear program, support for terrorism, and human rights abuses.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.

These designations are part of ongoing efforts to exert financial pressure on the Iranian regime and its affiliates, often targeting networks involved in proliferation, illicit finance, or human rights violations.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber and Criminal Organizations, Issues Cuba-Related Determination
body: On November 5, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations.

Concurrently, OFAC also issued new designations related to Cuba and published a Cuba-related determination, indicating a continued focus on restricting financial flows to the Cuban government and its associated entities, as well as combating illicit cyber activities and organized crime.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations, Venezuela General License Amendment
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, alongside updates to certain Iran-related listings.

Additionally, OFAC published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question, signaling adjustments to both Iranian and Venezuelan sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License.

General Licenses typically authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under sanctions programs, suggesting a potential modification or clarification of permissible activities involving Iran.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Related to North Korea and DRC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
These actions underscore the U.S. commitment to countering threats posed by North Korea's weapons of mass destruction programs and addressing human rights abuses and corruption in the DRC.

articles.headline: OFAC Reaches Settlement Agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc.
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.

This settlement indicates a resolution to alleged violations of OFAC sanctions regulations by the company, highlighting the importance of robust compliance programs for businesses operating internationally.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

These updates aim to provide further clarity and guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under OFAC regulations, ensuring proper compliance with sanctions requirements.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.

Concurrently, OFAC also issued Belarus and North Korea designations removals, along with new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions, indicating a dynamic and evolving sanctions landscape across multiple regions.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Associated General Licenses

These designations were accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses, indicating a targeted approach to safeguarding American intellectual property while providing specific authorizations for certain activities.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of 'Affiliates Rule' Until January 10, 2027
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has officially extended the suspension of its 'Affiliates Rule' until January 10, 2027.

This rule, initially set to take effect on November 9, 2026, would expand export control restrictions under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to companies owned or controlled by parties on certain restricted party lists, including the Entity List and Military End-User List.

The extension, published in the Federal Register on November 9, 2026, aligns with the ongoing U.S.-China trade truce and provides additional relief for exporters who would have faced significantly increased compliance obligations and enforcement risks.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
